headline: Microsoft is reported to be weighing cost cuts of at least 20 percent in a large division of its Azure cloud business, although Microsoft disputes the account.
score_reason: Lowered one point from the pool score: the headline overstates a division-level request, it rests on one anonymous source, and Microsoft disputes that any cuts were directed.
importance_line: Staff in a roughly 11,500-person Azure division, and outside contractors in particular, could be affected if cuts go ahead, and investors are watching how Microsoft pays for AI data centres, but the report rests on an anonymous source, Microsoft denies directing cuts, and it does not say whether jobs would go.
summary: The Information reports, citing a person with direct knowledge, that Girish Bablani, president of the Azure group that builds software for cloud servers, recently told leaders in his roughly 11,500-person division to propose cost savings of at least 20 percent, which could include parting with outside contractors, while the report does not say whether layoffs are being discussed. A Microsoft spokesperson disputed the account, saying "Azure leadership has not directed teams to develop cost-cutting plans", and Stocktwits notes the push comes as AI data-centre spending rises even though Azure's revenue grew 40 percent to $101.9 billion in the year to June.
notes: The Information page is paywalled; read the Stocktwits relay on TradingView and The Information's public teaser. The pool title says "Microsoft Cloud President"; the text gives Bablani as president of Azure's server-software group. Microsoft's denial is in the text.
